title: Startup and CLR services
sub: Who launches the program and what the CLR gives it
cards/0/title: The CLR is more than the JIT
cards/0/body:
While a program runs, the CLR provides services:

Garbage collection: frees memory that is no longer needed.
Safety: type and bounds checks.
Native interop: calling C and C++ libraries.
Cross-language debugging.
Deployment and versioning of libraries.
cards/1/pairs/1/0: Call a function from a C library
cards/1/pairs/2/0: A breakpoint in an F# library called from C#
cards/1/pairs/3/0: Two programs need different library versions
cards/2/body:
Here's how the Microsoft article describes it for .NET Framework:

The Windows loader sees a "this is a managed module" flag in the file header and loads mscoree.dll. The _CorValidateImage function checks that the file holds valid managed code and replaces the entry point with the CLR's entry point.
cards/2/deep: On 64-bit Windows, _CorValidateImage also converts the in-memory image from PE32 to PE32+. Its counterpart, _CorImageUnloading, tells the loader when the image is unloaded.
cards/3/q: Put the .NET Framework startup in order
cards/3/items/3: _CorValidateImage checks the code and swaps the entry point
cards/3/explain: First the OS, then mscoree.dll, an image check, and control passes to the CLR.
cards/4/body: The chain is the same on Windows, Linux and macOS. It starts with a tiny launcher, hello.exe (the apphost), or the command dotnet hello.dll.
cards/4/deep: hostfxr reads hello.runtimeconfig.json and picks a suitable installed runtime using roll-forward rules. hostpolicy reads hello.deps.json and builds the list of assemblies to load. Native AOT skips this chain: the file is native from the start.
cards/5/explain: Host, version choice, dependencies, CLR, your code.
cards/6/q: The computer has no .NET. Someone runs hello.exe, a regular build, not Native AOT. What do they see?
cards/6/options/0: A message saying .NET must be installed to run it
cards/6/options/2: Windows embeds the CLR into the file
cards/6/explain: hostfxr found no suitable runtime. The launcher shows "You must install or update .NET to run this application" with a download link.
cards/6/wrong/1: Without .NET installed, only Native AOT or a self-contained build, which carries the runtime with it, will start.
cards/7/q: Main calls Add for the first time. What happens?
cards/7/options/0: Stub, then JIT, then machine code, then execution
cards/7/options/1: The CPU runs the CIL directly
cards/7/options/2: The CLR reads and interprets the C# source
cards/7/options/3: Add was already compiled at install time
cards/7/explain: Each method is compiled on its first call and then executed. That goes on until the program ends.
cards/8/body: This is managed execution. You've walked through every step. All that's left is the final challenge.
